Do you have difficulty breathing because of the abdominal enlargement?
orders: Bedside abdominal examination with the patient supine and standing, including palpation of the umbilicus and entire abdominal wall, cough impulse, reducibility, and assessment for shifting dullness and fluid thrill
Abdominal-wall and complete abdominal ultrasound with Doppler
CT scan of the abdomen and pelvis with intravenous contrast
Complete blood count, comprehensive metabolic panel, liver enzymes, albumin, and coagulation profile
Upright and supine abdominal radiographs to assess bowel obstruction or colonic dilatation

Dynamic abdominal-wall ultrasound during quiet breathing, coughing, Valsalva, and partial sit-up, specifically assessing for occult ventral hernia, rectus diastasis, abdominal-wall mass, and muscle movement
Focused bedside abdominal examination with inspection, percussion for ascites, and palpation for a firm or fluid-filled distension
